land.text: the Territory of Papua: 'place our Possession of British New Guinea under the authority of the Commonwealth of Australia'

successors.note: Letters patent of 18 March 1902; the Papua Act 1905 (passed 16 November 1905) took effect on 1 September 1906.

correction.text: the protectorate 'from East Cape to the boundary of Dutch New Guinea in the west', bordering German New Guinea to the north: south-eastern New Guinea and its islands, here the six Papuan provinces Central, Gulf, Milne Bay, National Capital District, Northern and Western

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 718 cells, about 182,000 km2 by the gazetteer; the page gives no area. The split is the same province approximation as commonwealth-of-australia_1906 and german-new-guinea (no page gives the Anglo-German line: 'a draft agreement' in 1885, formalised in the 1886 Anglo-German Declarations). The Louisiade, D'Entrecasteaux and Trobriand islands are not on the page (inside Milne Bay province).

region.text: south-eastern New Guinea from East Cape to the Dutch New Guinea boundary

ledger.note: 1884: Britain proclaims a protectorate over south-eastern New Guinea (infobox 21 October 1884; 'A further proclamation and flag-raising ceremony was nonetheless held on 6 November, with Erskine presiding'). Queensland's own annexation by Chester at Port Moresby on 4 April 1883 had been repudiated. The page gives the protectorate 'from East Cape to the boundary of Dutch New Guinea in the west'; the province split is the researcher's.

1888: the protectorate becomes a Crown colony: 'On 4 September 1888, McGregor formally proclaimed the south-eastern portion of New Guinea as a Crown colony.' William MacGregor was appointed first administrator under letters patent of 8 June 1888. Same state, same colour (rule 2).

region.text: British New Guinea as it stood in 1906

ledger.note: 1906: British New Guinea becomes the Australian Territory of Papua. 'On 18 March 1902 ... King Edward VII issued letters patent to place our Possession of British New Guinea under the authority of the Commonwealth of Australia'; the Papua Act 1905 'provisions were not enacted until 1 September 1906'. The Territory of Papua is carried by commonwealth-of-australia.

certainty.note: Only the sea coast and the Dutch line are named; the northern boundary with the German protectorate was undefined until the 1885 draft.

The northern frontier is a treaty line: the 1885 draft agreement 'formalised in the 1886 Anglo-German Declarations' on the page; the Dutch boundary is not described, and the interior of the colony was unexplored for years.

sources.title: British New Guinea
sources.note: Protectorate 21 October 1884 and flag-raising 6 November, Queensland's 1883 annexation, the 1885 draft boundary with Germany and 1886 Declarations, Crown colony 4 September 1888, letters patent 18 March 1902, Papua Act 1 September 1906, capital Port Moresby. No area.

sources.title: Territorial evolution of Australia
sources.note: Queensland claimed south-eastern New Guinea on 4 April 1883; Britain declared a protectorate on 6 November 1884 (cross-check).

notes:
Written by oc-02-x. One page opened (British New Guinea); the Territorial evolution of Australia page (opened for the Australian colonies) dates the Queensland claim (4 April 1883) and the protectorate (6 November 1884).
Dates differ: the colony page's infobox gives 21 October 1884 (Romilly) for the protectorate and 6 November 1884 for the flag-raising; the Territorial evolution page gives 6 November 1884 for 'declared it a protectorate'. The Papua Act date (1 September 1906) matches commonwealth-of-australia's gain event, but the 1902 letters patent already placed the possession under Australian authority; the dossier ends at 1906 as the oc-02-a dossier starts the Territory of Papua then. Cliopatria's British Colonial Empire row (eu-11) still contains the land; the rendering should treat this colony as its child.
NOT ON THE PAGE. The area, the Dutch boundary longitude (141 E), the 1885 draft's text, MacGregor's later years, the place of Samarai, the Louisiade/D'Entrecasteaux/Trobriand islands and the Torres Strait border with Queensland. Page budget: one page for a 22-year state; the next step would be the 'Anglo-German Declarations' and 'Territory of Papua' pages.
